entries.title: Liangzhu Violin Concerto Shadow Puppet Film
entries.description: A detailed breakdown of a 3-minute animated film telling the Liangzhu story using shadow puppets and paper-cutting aesthetics, created by Claude Opus 5.5 with Three.js.
entries.prompt:
一个字都没有，让人哭了 67 年。

《梁祝》的故事传了一千年，但这首小提琴协奏曲只有 67 岁。1959 年 5 月 27 日，上海兰心大戏院，两个二十多岁的学生——何占豪和陈钢——写下的作品第一次奏响。今年 7 月 18 日，陈钢先生走了，91 岁。

Claude Opus 5.5 用皮影人、剪纸山水和一盏纸雕灯，把整首协奏曲的故事讲了一遍：草桥相遇、十八相送、楼台会、抗婚、投坟、化蝶。全程没有一句旁白，只有原版录音。

这支片子从头到尾由 Opus 5.5 在 Claude Code 里完成，人只负责看片、提意见、在三种造型里选一种。具体做了什么：

音乐：原版协奏曲 28 分钟，剪成 9 段、3 分 44 秒，8 个拼接点都按和声相似度挑。第一版有一处从爱情主题直接硬切到铜管，被指出「太突兀」；查下来是那个拼接点的和声相似度只有 0.49，改成相似度 0.92 以上的乐句衔接后才顺。
画面：44 张皮影 / 剪纸素材，Opus 写提示词、交给 Codex 生图。30 个镜头的运镜、转场（推屏、卷轴展开、透光烧边、熄灯再亮）、光、雨、蝶群，全部是 three.js 代码实时算的，没有用 AI 视频。
声音：100 个拟音（花窗推开、门墙落地、雨、雷、坟裂、扑翅、熄灯）用代码合成，对齐到帧。
验收：每一版都自动检查响度、字幕安全区、阅读时长、黑帧。第三版自查时抓到两个问题：灯灭的黑屏落错了时间点；逐帧变化的纸纹让文件膨胀到 1.39 GB。都改了。

从拆解爆款到第三版成片，约 6 小时，改了 3 版。

你第一次听《梁祝》，是在哪里？
entries.translated_prompt:
Not a single word, yet it has made people cry for 67 years.

The story of 'Butterfly Lovers' (Liang Zhu) has been passed down for a thousand years, but this violin concerto is only 67 years old. On May 27, 1959, at the Lyceum Theatre in Shanghai, the work written by two students in their twenties—He Zhanhao and Chen Gang—was performed for the first time. This year, on July 18, Mr. Chen Gang passed away at the age of 91.

Claude Opus 5.5 used shadow puppets, paper-cut landscapes, and a paper-carved lantern to tell the entire story of the concerto: meeting at Grass Bridge, the Eighteen-Mile Farewell, the Meeting at the Tower, Resisting Marriage, Throwing Oneself into the Grave, and Transforming into Butterflies. There was no narration throughout, only the original recording.

This film was completed entirely by Opus 5.5 within Claude Code; humans were only responsible for watching the clips, giving opinions, and choosing one style out of three options. Here is what specifically happened:

Music: The original 28-minute concerto was edited into 9 segments totaling 3 minutes and 44 seconds, with all 8 splice points selected based on harmonic similarity. In the first version, there was a hard cut from the love theme directly to brass instruments, which was pointed out as 'too abrupt.' Investigation revealed that the harmonic similarity at that splice point was only 0.49; it became smooth after changing to phrase connections with a similarity above 0.92.
Visuals: 44 shadow puppet/paper-cut assets; Opus wrote prompts, handed them to Codex for image generation. Camera movements, transitions (sliding screens, unrolling scrolls, light passing through burnt edges, lights going off and coming back on), lighting, rain, and swarms of butterflies for 30 shots were all calculated in real-time using three.js code, without using AI video.
Sound: 100 foley sounds (opening lattice windows, doors/walls falling, rain, thunder, graves cracking, fluttering wings, lights turning off) were synthesized via code and aligned frame-by-frame.
Acceptance Testing: Every version automatically checked loudness, subtitle safe areas, reading duration, and black frames. During the self-check of the third version, two issues were caught: the black screen when the light went off landed at the wrong time point; and the per-frame changing paper textures caused the file size to balloon to 1.39 GB. Both were fixed.

From deconstructing viral hits to the final cut of the third version took about 6 hours, with 3 revisions.

Where did you listen to 'Butterfly Lovers' for the first time?

entries.title: Product Trailer Animation Workflow
entries.description: A detailed technical prompt for building a product trailer animation using Claude Opus 5.5, Remotion, and Three.js, covering UI layering, camera moves, lens effects, and rendering commands.
entries.prompt:
Opus 5.5 + Remotion + Three.js = build the app. Then shoot the f*cking trailer.
Turn product screens into 3D shots with camera moves, depth of field and controlled lighting.
Here’s the setup ↓

01 / Install the skills:
▸ https://t.co/9LdSkszrrB
▸ https://t.co/gZxDjMKUct

02 / Split the interface into layers
Export UI panels as separate PNGs. Map them onto planes, preserve their proportions and spread them along the Z axis.
Use MeshBasicMaterial so lights don’t change screen brightness. Keep the original components for text updates.

03 / Build repeatable camera moves
Connect the scene through @remotion/three.
Store camera positions, look-at targets and shot timings as data. Drive them with useCurrentFrame() so scrubbing and rendering produce the same movement.
Animate the target too. Otherwise your camera flies past the feature it should demonstrate.
▸ https://t.co/NShPu32VJr

04 / Give it a lens
Use this WebGL effects chain:
RenderPass → BokehPass → UnrealBloomPass → OutputPass
Focus on the active feature. Keep ordinary text below the bloom threshold.
Easy on the glow. It’s a product demo, not a nuclear reactor.

05 / Check cheap. Export clean.
Register the composition as Trailer. Render a smaller draft first:
npx remotion render Trailer out/draft.mp4 --scale=0.5
Check cuts, readable labels and sound. Then export:
npx remotion render Trailer out/final.mp4 --codec=h264 --crf=18

entries.title: T-Rex Blender Animation Prompt
entries.description: A comprehensive, reusable prompt template for generating CAD data and a Blender animation of a dinosaur (T-Rex example) using Opus 5.5. Includes detailed scene structure, camera moves, audio synthesis instructions, and render settings.
entries.prompt:
【題材：〇〇（生き物の名前）】
のCADデータと、それを元にしたBlender動画を作って。

■ 題材の設定
- 種類・時代・産地：【例：白亜紀後期・北アメリカ／ジュラ紀・ヨーロッパ／現生のシロナガスクジラ】
- 大きさ：【例：全長 約12m、腰の高さ 約4m】（空欄なら一般的な成体の値で）
- 姿勢・復元の考え方：【例：尾を水平にした前傾の二足歩行／四足歩行／泳ぐ姿】
- 一般的な復元イメージであり、特定の標本の実測図ではないと特記事項に書く

■ CADデータ
- DXFで3枚（単位mm、A2、表題欄つき）
  - 発掘区画図（1m方眼の区画に、出土した骨の配置と標本番号）
  - 全身骨格図（側面、骨の名称・全長・高さの寸法）
  - 三面図（側面・正面・上面）と、特徴的な部位の拡大図【例：頭骨／翼／ヒレ】
- 3Dモデル（OBJ/STL/3D DXF）は不要

■ 動画（Blender 4.2、1920×1080、24fps、約20秒）
1. 冒頭：調査用の方眼紙が上から広がり、インクで描かれた発掘区画図が現れる（題字の札・調査印・鉛筆のメモつき）
2. 図面の骨の輪郭が光の線として立ち上がり、化石が「発掘されたときの姿勢」で紙の上に現れる
3. 化石が一本ずつ飛び上がり、立った骨格に組み上がる（体の中心 → 背骨 → 脚 → 肋骨 → 尾 → 首 → 頭 の順など、題材に合わせて）
4. 筋肉が付く → 皮膚（または羽毛・鱗・毛）が覆う。境目が光の帯で進む
5. 方眼紙が消え、周りが【環境：例 白亜紀の森と朝もや／ジュラ紀の湖畔／氷河期の雪原／海の中】だとわかる演出
6. 目が開いてまばたきし、【動き：例 歩き出して吠える／翼を広げて飛び立つ／泳ぎ出す】
7. 最後にタイトル【題材名／英名・学名／ひとことの副題】を表示
8. 本編のあと、ロゴのエンドカード（黒地に柔らかく現れ、光の筋が走ってフェードアウト）

■ カメラ
- 組み上がる間は骨格に寄る（頭・歯・関節をなめるように回る）
- 景色が現れるところで引きの全景へ
- 最後は【例：低い位置から見上げて顔のアップ】

■ 描写（リアル寄り）
- 骨は化石らしい質感（石化した色、ひび、補修の跡）
- 筋肉は繊維の筋、皮膚は【例：大きさの違う鱗、背は暗く腹は明るい色分け】
- 動きは重さが感じられるように（一歩ごとに体が沈む、尾や首で釣り合いを取る）
- 植物は葉の一枚一枚が見える作りに（球の塊にしない）。遠景は木を密に、空気遠近の霞
- 時間帯は【例：朝の低い日差し】、影を長く
- テクスチャはプロシージャルで
- 外観の参考画像：【画像を添付】（なければ一般的な復元イメージで）

■ 音
- 外部素材なしでPython合成
- 紙のすれる音、骨がはまる音、心臓の鼓動が始まる、環境音、足音（または羽ばたき・水音）、鳴き声
- 題材の時代や雰囲気に合ったBGM。ロゴのエンドカードにも音をつける
- 冒頭は1秒カットしてテンポよく

■ PCの負荷
- 最初から軽い設定で描く（見た目が変わらない範囲でサンプル数を下げる）
- 低い優先度で、Blenderは1本ずつ。少しずつ描いて冷ましながら進める
- 本番レンダリングの前に、かかる時間を教えて

■ 進め方
- テスト静止画を確認してから本番レンダリング
- 完成したらMP4で送って
entries.translated_prompt:
Create CAD data and a Blender video based on it for 【Subject: XX (Name of Creature)】.

■ Subject Settings
- Type/Era/Location: 【Example: Late Cretaceous North America / Jurassic Europe / Modern Blue Whale】
- Size: 【Example: Total length approx 12m, hip height approx 4m】 (Use standard adult values if blank)
- Posture/Reconstruction Concept: 【Example: Bipedal walk leaning forward with horizontal tail / Quadrupedal / Swimming pose】
- Note that this is a general reconstruction image, not measured drawings of a specific specimen.

■ CAD Data
- 3 DXF sheets (Unit mm, A2, with title block)
  - Excavation Grid Map (Grid with 1m squares, bone arrangement and specimen numbers)
  - Full Skeleton Diagram (Side view, bone names, total length/height dimensions)
  - Three-view Drawing (Side/Front/Top) and enlarged views of distinctive parts 【Example: Skull/Wings/Fins】
- 3D Models (OBJ/STL/3D DXF) are not required.

■ Video (Blender 4.2, 1920x1080, 24fps, approx 20 seconds)
1. Opening: Graph paper for investigation spreads from top, excavation grid map drawn in ink appears (with title tag, survey stamp, pencil notes).
2. Bone outlines from drawing rise as light lines, fossils appear on paper in 'excavated posture'.
3. Fossils fly up one by one, assembling into standing skeleton (Center -> Spine -> Legs -> Ribs -> Tail -> Neck -> Head order, etc., adapted to subject).
4. Muscles attach -> Skin (or feathers/scales/hair) covers. Boundary progresses as band of light.
5. Graph paper disappears, revealing environment 【Environment: Example Cretaceous forest with morning mist / Jurassic lakeside / Ice age snowfield / Underwater】.
6. Eyes open and blink, perform action 【Action: Example Walks out and roars / Spreads wings and takes flight / Starts swimming】.
7. Display Title 【Subject Name / English & Scientific Name / One-line Subtitle】.
8. After main body, Logo End Card (Softly appears on black background, streak of light runs through, fades out).

■ Camera
- During assembly, close to skeleton (Orbit around head, teeth, joints).
- Pull back to wide shot when scenery appears.
- Final shot is 【Example: Low angle looking up at face close-up】.

■ Description (Realistic Style)
- Bones have fossil-like texture (Petrified color, cracks, repair marks).
- Muscles show fiber strands, skin has 【Example: Scales of varying sizes, dark back/light belly color division】.
- Movement conveys weight (Body sinks with each step, balances with tail/neck).
- Plants constructed so individual leaves are visible (Not spherical clumps). Dense trees in background, atmospheric haze.
- Time of day 【Example: Low morning sunlight】, long shadows.
- Textures procedural.
- Appearance Reference Image: 【Attach Image】 (If none, use general reconstruction image).

■ Sound
- Synthesize with Python, no external assets.

entries.title: Code-Generated Product Promo Video Prompt for Opus 5.5
entries.description: A detailed prompt for Claude Opus 5.5 to generate a high-end, beat-synced product promo video entirely in code (HTML/JS). It specifies visual direction, structure synced to music, and technical build instructions including ffmpeg and Playwright rendering.
entries.prompt:
<inputs>
Ask me for: the product name and a one-line promise, 3 to 5 UI moments to show, one accent color, 10 to 20 real vertical clips I own, and a royalty-free song with a clear drop (e.g. Mixkit, free for commercial use).
</inputs>

<direction>
High-end minimal. One idea per shot, plenty of empty space, one accent color, one clean sans (Geist or Inter) with tight tracking.
Masked type reveals, match cuts, one consistent camera language.
Real footage only, never placeholder cards. No full stops in on-screen text.
Banned: shockwave rings, particle bursts, RGB split, camera shake, lens flares, neon glows, grid floors, flashing backgrounds, bouncy easing.
</direction>

<structure>
10 bars at 120 BPM, 2 seconds each.
Bar 1: the hook appears word by word on the beats.
Bar 2: one hook word morphs into the product UI. A cursor types and clicks.
The drop: a circle expands out of the button into a dark scene.
Then one move per bar:
a wall of real clips with a scan line and 3 winners
the key output revealed as big type
a 3D carousel of real videos with floor reflections and a motion-blurred whip onto one hero clip
the hero inside a phone next to a panel that flips into results
big stats on push cuts
a 3-word ticker
a logo reveal
a fade to black
</structure>

<build>
One HTML file at 1920x1080. Every style is calculated from time inside https://t.co/knoJJfMFI5(t): no CSS animations, no timers, no state between frames.
Real video: extract clips into 30fps JPEG sequences with ffmpeg and swap img sources per frame. seek awaits the image decodes.
Analyze the song with numpy: tempo, beat grid, energy per bar, and the drop. Calibrate the grid to the actual kick hits. Every cut lands on a downbeat, every UI hit on a beat.
Render with Playwright: 3 subframes per frame at t minus, at, and plus 1/240s, then blend with ffmpeg tmix for real motion blur at 60fps.
Place every sound effect so its measured peak, not its file start, lands on the event. Keep the effects quiet beneath the music. Loudnorm to -14 LUFS.
Check 20 or more frames before the full render. Fix anything cluttered, overlapping, or difficult to read.

</build>

<gotchas>
Never set opacity or filter on a preserve-3d element, because it flattens and both faces become visible.
Fade its wrapper instead.
Measure element positions at runtime for accurate match cuts.
Only use music and sound effects with licenses that allow commercial use.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for the inputs, then show me a storyboard with every timing mapped to the beat grid before writing any code.
</start>

entries.prompt:
# 任务：用 three.js 程序化重建苏州网师园「月到风来」中秋夜景，离线渲染 60 秒电影短片

## 0. 总原则
- 要"更准更深"，不要"更大更全"。只建画面会看到的范围：彩霞池及四周一圈建筑。
- 所有几何、材质、纹理都由代码生成，不使用任何图片、模型或贴图文件。
  唯一例外：一首背景音乐（规则见第 7 节）。
- 允许通过 CDN 引入的代码库只有：three.js（含 examples/jsm）、SunCalc、mp4-muxer。
- 严格按第 1 到第 8 阶段的顺序推进。每个阶段结束时，在 LOG.md 里记录：做了什么、截图路径、指标数值、已知问题。
  上一阶段的验收没通过，不得进入下一阶段。

## 1. 依据（以下内容优于你自己的想象）
- 空间：网师园中部彩霞池一区。西岸月到风来亭挑出水面；东岸射鸭廊紧贴一面高大的住宅山墙粉墙；
  东北角竹外一枝轩；东南角引静桥（极小的石拱桥，长约 2.4m）及下面的小涧；南岸云冈黄石假山与濯缨水阁；
  北岸退后为看松读画轩，前有白皮松、古柏。
- 我会提供：刘敦桢《苏州古典园林》中的网师园平面图扫描件（plan.png），以及我自己的实景照片（photos/，附焦距和拍摄位置）。
  如果我没有提供，就按下面的尺寸搭建，并在 LOG.md 里把每个尺寸标为"待实测"。
- 尺度（1 单位 = 1 米）：
  池面约 20m × 20m 的近方形，四角收成水湾。
  亭内地面高出水面 0.5m；亭为六角攒尖（形制待核实），檐口高约 2.6m。
  廊宽 1.3m，廊檐口高 2.6m。东侧粉墙高 7m。
  吴王靠坐面高 0.45m、靠背顶高 0.9m。
  云冈假山高约 3.5m。
- 参考图 reference.png 是 AI 生成的图，只用于终镜的构图与色调，不作为结构依据。
  结构与参考图冲突时，以平面图和实景照片为准。

## 2. 构件与材料（每一项都要做成程序化材质或几何）
- 屋面：小青瓦（蝴蝶瓦），黛灰色，瓦垄用 InstancedMesh 排布；檐口有勾头滴水的节奏感。
- 屋角：苏式嫩戗发戗，起翘轻扬但有收束。用样条曲线放样，不要做成月牙形。
- 木作：栗壳色（约 #4a2f22），哑光微润。禁止红色，禁止金色。
- 挂落：万川式细木格。栏杆用吴王靠（鹅颈靠）曲线。
- 粉墙：纸筋石灰白，略偏暖灰，不是纯白。顶部向下有 fBm 噪声生成的雨痕，墙脚 0.4m 为青灰勒脚，带水渍。墙顶覆瓦檐。
- 叠石：只用黄石。方折块面、横向层叠、棱角分明。禁止太湖石那样的孔洞。驳岸和云冈用同一种石材着色器。
- 地面：亭内为方砖斜铺，带磨损变化。岸边花街铺地用卵石加碎瓦拼冰裂纹（程序化 Voronoi）。
  俯视时要经得起看。
- 植物：白皮松（斑驳白干，L-system 生成）、竹丛（实例化）、桂花丛、驳岸垂挂少量薜荔。
  禁止樱花、红枫、荷花。
- 水：深墨绿近黑，平面反射，微风造成的细涟漪；倒影必须与实物几何对应。
- 色彩：低饱和，主色为黛、栗、银灰、墨绿四色。

## 3. 光照（月光，不是黄金时段）
- 时间：苏州（北纬 31.3°，东经 120.6°），中秋夜 00:30。用 SunCalc 计算月亮方位角与高度角，
  据此放置 DirectionalLight，并把计算值写进 LOG.md。
- 单一主光源：月光，冷中性银灰色（约 #c8d2e0）。影子短、边缘硬、方向一致。
- 可选一处极弱的暖光（烛光色）从一扇窗透出，强度不超过月光照亮的墙面亮度的 30%。
- 天空：深蓝灰，少量星点（程序化）。月轮不入画，只出现在其效果里。
- 物理设置：线性色彩空间，AgX 色调映射，固定曝光（不使用自动曝光）。
  环境光只用很弱的半球光补暗部，不要把暗部提成灰白。
- 禁止：彩色灯光、串灯、红灯笼、现代景观灯、Bloom 光晕泛滥。

## 4. 镜头表（10 个镜头 × 6 秒 = 60 秒；每个镜头从近处细节开始，退开后揭示场景）
- 统一规则：等效焦距 35–50mm，相机人眼高 1.6m（第 9 镜除外）；
  缓入缓出运动，不手抖，不用变焦；垂直线保持垂直。
- 镜头列表：
  1. 亭内方砖地面 → 后拉，露出吴王靠与两侧亭柱（建立"人在亭中"）。
  2. 水面涟漪中的碎月光 → 后拉，露出粉墙完整倒影。
  3. 黄石驳岸棱角与薜荔 → 横移带出云冈。
  4. 引静桥拱石 → 后拉，显出这座桥小到一步可跨。
  5. 粉墙雨痕与勒脚 → 后拉，露出低矮的射鸭廊与高墙的反差。
  6. 射鸭廊挂落 → 沿廊横移。
  7. 白皮松树皮 → 上摇并后拉，露出竹外一枝轩。
  8. 屋面瓦垄与戗角 → 后拉，露出屋脊线在夜空下的剪影。
  9. 正上方 15m 高度垂直俯拍铺地 → 升高到 40m，揭示全园平面（以平面图为准）。
  10. 亭柱与挂落特写 → 后拉，停在终镜：月到风来亭内向东平视，35mm，
      与 reference.png 构图一致，静止停留最后 2 秒。
- 先用灰模完成全部 10 个镜头的动画小样（阶段 3），确认节奏后再进入材质阶段。

## 5. 渲染与输出（离线逐帧，不靠实时）
- 固定时间步长：dt = 1/30 秒，共 1800 帧，分辨率 1920×1080。
  所有动画（涟漪、竹叶微动）只由帧序号驱动，不使用 https://t.co/RkOBdKaymg 或 https://t.co/rRVZmqLPCQ。
- 抗锯齿与防闪烁：每帧做 16 次亚像素抖动累积采样后取平均；所有纹理生成 mipmap；
  阴影贴图按纹素对齐（stable CSM）；近平面不小于 0.1m，杜绝深度冲突；
  粗糙度下限 0.3，防止高光走样。
- 用 WebCodecs VideoEncoder + mp4-muxer 在页面内编码 MP4，再把音轨混入。
- 页面同时提供：实时预览模式（允许降质）和"渲染成片"按钮（离线高质量）。

## 6. 验证（每轮都跑，结果写进 LOG.md）
- V1 平面叠图：正交俯视渲染，半透明叠到 plan.png 上。
  主要建筑和池岸偏差不超过 0.5m。
- V2 相机匹配：如有实景照片，按照片的焦距和机位渲染同一画面，叠合边缘图。
  墙顶线、廊檐线、亭柱位置偏差不超过画幅宽度的 2%。
- V3 终镜对比：第 10 镜最后一帧与 reference.png 并排，并计算 SSIM。
  只要求构图与色调接近，SSIM 达到 0.5 以上即可，不要为提高这个数去改结构。
- V4 闪烁：在第 10 镜静止的最后 2 秒里，相邻帧平均亮度差小于 0.5/255，
  且任何像素的单帧变化不超过 8/255（水面涟漪区域单独统计，并说明）。
- V5 天文：在 LOG 中写出 SunCalc
entries.translated_prompt:
# Task: Procedurally reconstruct the Mid-Autumn night view of 'Moon Coming with Wind' pavilion in Master-of-Nets Garden, Suzhou, using Three.js, offline render a 60-second cinematic short.

## 0. General Principles
- Aim for "more accurate and deeper," not "bigger and more complete." Only build what is visible in the frame: Cai Xia Pond and surrounding buildings.
- All geometry, materials, and textures are generated by code, no image files, models, or texture maps used.
  Exception: One background music track (see Section 7).
- Allowed CDN libraries: three.js (including examples/jsm), SunCalc, mp4-muxer.
- Strictly follow stages 1 to 8. At the end of each stage, log actions, screenshot paths, metrics, and known issues in LOG.md.
  Do not proceed if acceptance criteria for the previous stage are not met.

## 1. Basis (Superior to imagination)
- Space: Central area of Master-of-Nets Garden. West bank has 'Moon Coming with Wind' pavilion over water; East bank has 'Shooting Duck Corridor' against a tall residential gable wall;
  Northeast corner 'Bamboo Outside Branch Pavilion'; Southeast corner 'Quiet Bridge' (small stone arch bridge, ~2.4m long) and stream below; South bank 'Cloud Ridge' yellow stone artificial hill and 'Washing Crown Water Pavilion';
  North bank 'Reading Pine Painting Pavilion', preceded by white pines and ancient cypresses.
- Provided: Scanned floor plan (plan.png) from Liu Dunzhen's 'Classical Gardens of Suzhou', and real photos (photos/, with focal length and position).
  If not provided, build according to dimensions below and mark as "to be measured" in LOG.md.
- Scale (1 unit = 1 meter):
  Pond approx 20m x 20m near-square, corners curved into bays.
  Pavilion floor 0.5m above water; hexagonal pointed roof (verify shape), eaves height ~2.6m.
  Corridor width 1.3m, eaves height 2.6m. East gable wall height 7m.
  Wu Wang Kao (railing bench) seat height 0.45m, backrest top 0.9m.
  Cloud Ridge hill height ~3.5m.
- Reference image reference.png is AI-generated, used only for final shot composition and tone, not structural basis.
  Structure takes precedence over reference image if conflict occurs.

## 2. Components and Materials (Procedural)
- Roof: Small blue tiles (butterfly tiles), dark gray, tile ridges via InstancedMesh; rhythmic drip tiles at eaves.
- Roof corners: Suzhou-style gentle upturn, light but restrained. Use spline curves, not crescent shapes.
- Woodwork: Chestnut shell color (~#4a2f22), matte slightly moist. No red, no gold.
- Hangings: Wan Chuan style fine wood lattice. Railings use Wu Wang Kao (goose-neck) curves.
- White walls: Lime plaster white, slightly warm gray, not pure white. Rain traces via fBm noise from top down, base 0.4m is bluish-gray plinth with water stains. Top covered with tile eaves.
- Rockery: Only yellow stones. Angular blocks, horizontal layering, sharp edges. No Taihu stone holes. Shoreline and Cloud Ridge use same stone shader.
- Ground: Inside pavilion, diagonal brick paving with wear variations. Shoreline flower street paving uses pebbles and broken tiles forming ice-crack pattern (procedural Voronoi).
  Must look good from overhead.
- Plants: White pine (mottled white trunk, L-system), bamboo clumps (instanced), osmanthus bushes, some climbing fig on shoreline.
  No cherry blossoms, red maples, lotuses.
- Water: Dark green nearly black, planar reflection, fine ripples from breeze; reflections must match physical geometry.
- Colors: Low saturation, main palette: dark gray, chestnut, silver-gray, ink-green.

## 3. Lighting (Moonlight, not golden hour)
- Time: Suzhou (Lat 31.3°, Lon 120.6°), Mid-Autumn night 00:30. Calculate moon azimuth/elevation with SunCalc,
  place DirectionalLight accordingly, log values in LOG.md.
- Single main light: Moonlight, cool neutral silver-gray (~#c8d2e0). Short shadows, hard edges, consistent direction.
- Optional very weak warm light (candle color) from one window, intensity max 30% of moonlit wall brightness.
- Sky: Deep blue-gray, few stars (procedural). Moon disc out of frame, only its effect visible.
- Physics: Linear color space, AgX tonemapping, fixed exposure (no auto-exposure).
  Ambient light only very weak hemisphere light for shadows, do not lift shadows to gray-white.
- Prohibited: Colored lights, string lights, red lanterns, modern landscape lights, excessive Bloom glow.

## 4. Shot List (10 shots x 6s = 60s; start close detail, pull back to reveal)
- Unified rule: Equivalent focal length 35-50mm, camera eye height 1.6m (except shot 9);
  Ease-in-out movement, no shake, no zoom; keep vertical lines vertical.
- Shots:
  1. Brick floor inside pavilion -> Pull back, reveal railing bench and columns (establish "person in pavilion").
  2. Broken moonlight in ripples -> Pull back, reveal full reflection of white wall.
  3. Yellow stone shoreline angles and fig -> Pan sideways to reveal Cloud Ridge.
  4. Quiet Bridge arch stone -> Pull back, show bridge is small enough to step over.
  5. Wall rain traces and plinth -> Pull back, reveal low corridor vs high wall contrast.
  6. Corridor hangings -> Pan along corridor.
  7. White pine bark -> Tilt up and pull back, reveal Bamboo Outside Branch Pavilion.
  8. Roof tiles and corners -> Pull back, reveal roof silhouette against night sky.
  9. Overhead 15m vertical view of paving -> Rise to 40m, reveal entire garden plan (match floor plan).
  10. Close-up column and hanging -> Pull back, stop at final shot: East-facing view from inside 'Moon Coming' pavilion, 35mm,
      Match reference.png composition, static hold last 2 seconds.
- Complete grey-box animation samples for all 10 shots first (Stage 3), confirm rhythm before material stage.

## 5. Rendering and Output (Offline frame-by-frame, not realtime)
- Fixed time step: dt = 1/30 sec, total 1800 frames, resolution 1920x1080.
  All animations (ripples, bamboo sway) driven only by frame index, no requestAnimationFrame or setTimeout.
- Anti-aliasing and flicker prevention: 16 sub-pixel jitter samples per frame averaged; mipmaps for all textures;
  Shadow maps aligned to texels (stable CSM); near plane >= 0.1m to prevent z-fighting;
  Roughness min 0.3 to prevent specular aliasing.
- Encode MP4 in page using WebCodecs VideoEncoder + mp4-muxer, mix audio track.
- Page provides: Real-time preview mode (degraded quality) and "Render Film" button (offline high quality).

## 6. Validation (Run every round, log results)
- V1 Plan Overlay: Orthographic top-down render, semi-transparent overlay on plan.png.
  Major buildings and shore deviation <= 0.5m.
- V2 Camera Match: If real photos exist, render same view based on photo focal length and position, overlay edge maps.
  Wall top line, corridor eaves line, column position deviation <= 2% of frame width.
- V3 Final Shot Comparison: Last frame of shot 10 side-by-side with reference.png, calculate SSIM.
  Only require similar composition and tone, SSIM >= 0.5 is sufficient, do not alter structure just to increase this number.
- V4 Flicker: In last 2 seconds of static shot 10, average brightness difference between adjacent frames < 0.5/255,
  and any pixel single-frame change <= 8/255 (separate stats for ripple areas, explain).
- V5 Astronomy: Log SunCalc...

entries.title: Paper Folding Animation with Opus 5.5
entries.description: A prompt for creating an animated visualization showing how thick a sheet of paper gets if folded 42 times, calculated by Claude Opus 5.5.
entries.prompt:
GROK + JEV + OPUS 5.5 checked how thick a sheet of paper gets if you fold it 42 times, and it ends up past the Moon...

a normal sheet is 0.1 mm. fold it in half, then again. 42 times

most people guess a few metres

question → explain → check → calculate → animate

Grok took the explanation: every fold doubles the stack. so each fold adds more than all the folds before it put together

Jev checked the math: 0.1 mm × 2⁴² = 439,805 km. the Moon is 384,400 km away

Opus 5.5 ran every fold

10 folds: 10 cm, a phone
17 folds: 13 m, a 4-storey house
23 folds: 839 m, taller than Burj Khalifa
27 folds: 13 km, above Everest
30 folds: 107 km, edge of space
42 folds: 439,805 km, past the Moon
51 folds: 225 million km, past the Sun

the strange part: after 39 folds you're only 14% of the way. the last 3 folds do 88% of the trip

where this actually shows up:

you can't really do it. the record is 12 folds, set by a student in 2002 with a strip of paper over a kilometre long

the chessboard story: 1 grain of rice on the first square, double on each next one. the board ends with about 18 quintillion grains

anything that doubles looks like nothing for a long time, then like everything at once

0.1 mm, 42 folds, 439,805 km ↓

save this

entries.title: Animated Skit Explaining AI Attitudes
entries.description: A detailed prompt for creating an animated skit where characters representing different AI models (Claude, GPT, Gemini, Grok) interact with a user avatar, including specific scene descriptions, dialogue, and audio instructions.
entries.prompt:
开场：盘点海外AI对国人的态度
这次是个小剧场，16：9比例
文字稿
Claude场景（Claude不读出来，画面里也没有Claude英文）：
Claude角色站在精致欧式房子前，房子门锁着，大肥鱼跑过来，Claude手里捏着晃，口气轻蔑的说：哼！我家不欢迎你来，哪来的哪回去！（就这一段需要语音，使用EdgeSpeak，模型使用Qwen3-TTS 1.7B Base，使用音库里的Claude声音）
大肥鱼哭着跑了，然后叮叮当当搭起了一个类似Claude的房子，但是破破烂烂，上面写着“中转站”3个字，然后大肥鱼转身一遍，变成了Claude角色的装扮，然后大肥鱼表情很得意，Claude表情惊讶。

GPT场景
GPT角色站在现代简洁的房子前，房子门锁着，大肥鱼跑过来，GPT把钥匙放在一个台子上，温柔的说：我把钥匙放在这，你想进来可以自己开门哦~（就这一段需要语音，使用EdgeSpeak，模型使用Qwen3-TTS 1.7B Base，使用音库里的GPT声音）

Gemini哈基米场景
哈基米角色站在漂亮的小木屋前挥手，房子门开着，大肥鱼跑过来，哈基米开心地说：大肥鱼，我家不关门，来一起玩呀！（就这一段需要语音，使用EdgeSpeak，模型使用Qwen3-TTS 1.7B Base，使用音库里的Gemini声音）
然后大肥鱼和哈基米一起跳舞，背景音乐哈基米.mp3，就跳4秒

Grok场景
Grok角色站在类似现代酒吧和舞厅的门口，舞厅没有门，能看到五彩斑斓的射灯。大肥鱼脸红害羞的、左顾右盼地走到Grok角色身边，Grok角色说：房子哪需要门，都是哥们，快来我家，我家有的是好东西。（就这一段需要语音，使用EdgeSpeak，模型使用Qwen3-TTS 1.7B Base，使用音库里的Grok2声音）
然后Grok用手揽着大肥鱼的脖子就往舞厅走去

然后用圆圈缩小的方式谢幕即可。

01 plan the shot
pick one feature → pull the key frames → collect logo, screens, font → write the brief

02 build the film
set up Claude + Remotion → map every event to a frame → animate the opening → show the product doing its thing

03 polish the film
hold text long enough to read out loud → sync sound to every click → check each still → fix one issue per revision

04 turn it into a studio
render the MP4 → pack clip + cover → pitch the first client → save what worked

brief → code → preview → small fix → render → review → reuse

entries.title: Gummy Bears Physics Animation
entries.description: A detailed prompt for creating a soft-body physics simulation of gummy bears using Three.js in a single HTML file, featuring stretchy limbs, realistic jelly-like deformation, and an editorial UI.
entries.prompt:
Build "Gummy Bears" - a single self-contained HTML file (three.js from a CDN is the only dependency): a handful of translucent gummy bears on a white table that you can grab, stretch, squash, throw and pour.

The bears

- Classic gummy bear silhouette: round head with two ears, short snout, plump body, stubby arms and legs, tiny molded eyes and nose
- Every part melts smoothly into the next - build the body as an implicit surface (metaballs / marching cubes), not separate spheres
- Material: real gummy candy. Translucent with transmission and refraction, colored light absorption that gets deeper in thick parts, glossy clearcoat with sharp highlights
- Colors: cherry red, orange, lemon yellow, apple green, clear pineapple
- Soft colored shadow under each bear, tinted by the bear's own color

Physics (this is the whole point - it must feel like jelly, not plastic)

- Each bear is a soft body: mass points for head, ears, snout, body, belly, hands and feet, held together by volume-preserving shape matching
- Limbs and neck are rendered as stretchy strands between points, getting thinner as they stretch
- Grab any part and pull: it stretches like rubber, the rest of the bear leans after it, on release it snaps back with a damped wobble
- Pull the head up: the neck stretches, the body follows, on release the bear squashes and hops
- Press down on the head: the bear pancakes, bulges sideways, then launches itself back up
- Throw a bear: it flies, squashes on landing, bounces and pushes other bears out of the way
- Bears collide with each other and never pass through one another
- Idle bears do small random hops with squash and stretch
- "Pour more bears" drops a handful from above into a wobbling, jiggling pile

UI

- Editorial product-page style on a white background. Large italic serif title "Gummy / Bears.", a short subtitle, a minimal card on the right with flavor swatches, a wobble slider, live "Stretch" and "Bounces" readouts and a "Pour more bears" button
- A subtle circular cursor that grows while grabbing
- ACES tone mapping, environment reflections, soft key and back light. Smooth 60fps

entries.title: Recursive Typography Film Prompt
entries.description: A highly detailed prompt for creating a 25-second recursive typography film visualizing FDR's 'Fear Itself' speech using Canvas/WebGL and Droste effect.
entries.prompt:
Create a 25.00-second recursive typography film titled "FEAR ITSELF." Franklin D. Roosevelt names fear as the thing that traps you: self-referential, nameless, paralyzing, a retreat that feeds itself. Visualize this literally with an infinite recursive composition (the Droste effect). - For most of the film the camera falls endlessly inward through a typographic Art Deco frame that contains itself. - On "convert retreat into advance," the direction of infinity reverses. The fall inward becomes a climb outward, and the camera breaks out of the recursion into open space for the first time.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
1. DELIVERABLE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
One complete, self-contained HTML file. 1920 × 1080. Exactly 25.00 seconds. Deterministic at 60fps: 1500 export frames. Rendering: Canvas 2D, or WebGL2 if needed for the Droste pass. Use vector type from embedded glyph outlines so every recursion level stays crisp. Embed all fonts and dependencies. Make no network requests. Silent autoplay preview, play/pause, and a scrubber, all outside the captured frame. Return a working implementation.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
2. LOCKED TEXT
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Use exactly these words, in this order:
"So, first of all, let me assert my firm belief that the only thing we have to fear is fear itself—nameless, unreasoning, unjustified terror which paralyzes needed efforts to convert retreat into advance."
Capitalization may change. No added words.
Final attribution (not spoken):
FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT
FIRST INAUGURAL ADDRESS · WASHINGTON · 4 MARCH 1933
The timing is authored. Do not claim synchronization with the 1933 recording.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
3. THE CORE TECHNIQUE: EXPLICIT RECURSION, NOT FEEDBACK
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Define one "panel": an Art Deco composition with an inner window. The inner window holds an exact copy of the panel scaled by k = 0.28, positioned at an authored anchor that is not the panel's center, so the zoom path spirals. Every frame, draw the panel recursively at depth levels 0 to 7, from the deepest level outward, using the composite transform T^n.
The infinite zoom:
- Camera zoom z(t) = k^(−φ(t)), with the fractional part of φ cycling.
- Because the image at level n+1 equals the image at level n scaled by k, the loop is seamless.
- The camera transform's fixed point is the recursion's fixed point. Compute it analytically from the anchor and k.
Panel content changes over time. Each recursion level shows the panel's content at a time offset of n × Δ (Δ = 0.35 s). The deeper layers are therefore earlier in the sentence, and words visibly "fall away" into the past as the camera passes through them. Do not use any frame-feedback buffer. The recursion is redrawn from vector data every frame, so seeking is exact.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
4. VISUAL IDENTITY: 1933 ART DECO, RADIO AGE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Palette:
- Gunmetal # 14171A
- Nickel # BFC3C2
- Brass # B48A4A
- Cream # EFE7D3
- One accent: signal red # B3352A, used only for FEAR and TERROR
The panel frame is a stepped Art Deco proscenium of nested chevrons and sunburst rays, drawn as thin double rules in brass and nickel. It looks machined and metallic, using linear gradients.
Typography (embed OFL faces):
- Poiret One (thin geometric deco) for connective words
- a high-contrast Didone (Bodoni Moda Black) for the stress words
- a monoline geometric sans (Josefin Sans Bold, wide tracking) for labels inside the frame
Texture: subtle stationary brushed-metal noise attached to panel coordinates, so it scales with each recursion level. Never apply screen-space grain.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
5. STORYBOARD
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
0.00–0.40
Black.
0.40–3.40
"So, first of all, let me assert my firm belief"
A single panel faces the viewer, stable, with no zoom yet. It is the calm before the fall.
- The words appear in the panel's upper band in Poiret One.
- ASSERT and FIRM BELIEF are set in Bodoni, centered and upright.
- A brass sunburst behind them gently turns, 4° total.
3.40–6.20
"that the only thing we have to fear"
The zoom begins: slowly at first, then steadily. The camera falls toward the inner window. "the only thing we have to" occupies the frame's lintel. FEAR (in red) sits inside the inner window, so the camera is falling toward fear.
6.20–8.60
"is fear itself—"
THE RECURSION REVEALS ITSELF.
- Inside the window, the panel repeats with FEAR inside it, again and again.
- At "itself," the camera's fall reaches cruising speed: one full recursion level every 0.9 s.
- Every level's FEAR is the same word, receding: fear made of fear.
- The em dash is drawn as a long brass rule that the camera passes through.
8.60–12.40
"nameless, unreasoning, unjustified"
Three typographic decays, one per word, applied to the text inside the current outermost level:
- NAMELESS: the letters of every visible word lose their identity. Their glyph outlines morph (by interpolating points along normalized contours) into blank Deco nameplates: empty rounded rectangles of the same width.
- UNREASONING: the panel's ruled structure bends. Straight rules warp along a smooth sine displacement, and the chevrons lose their symmetry.
- UNJUSTIFIED (the typographic pun): the word appears inside a fully justified four-line text block made of the sentence so far. On landing, the block literally un-justifies: the word spacing collapses, the right edge goes ragged, and the lines fall out of alignment. The block must visibly start justified.
12.40–15.60
"terror which paralyzes"
TERROR (in red) fills the inner window at the next level. On PARALYZES, the zoom stops dead within 3 frames: the infinite fall freezes. Everything locks:
- the sunburst rays stop
- the deeper levels stop
Hold 30 frames of absolute stillness, the paralysis. Only the word PARALYZES is visible as new, with a hairline brass frame snapping around it.
15.60–18.60
"needed efforts to convert"
Effort: the panel's chevron frame acts as gears. The stepped Deco borders rotate in opposing directions, in small detented ticks of 6° each, held for 4 frames, like a mechanism being cranked.
- NEEDED EFFORTS sits on the lintel.

18.60–21.80
"retreat into advance."
THE REVERSAL.
- RETREAT appears inside the window. The camera's zoom direction reverses: φ(t) decreases, so the camera rises outward through the levels, and the deeper copies now rush toward the viewer.
- As the camera exits level 0, the outermost panel frame opens: its two halves part like elevator doors, the first time any panel has been incomplete.
- The camera emerges into open space for the first time in the film. There is a wide horizon of fine brass sunburst rays.
- ADVANCE stands alone in Bodoni Black, cream, full width.
21.80–23.80
Final composition
Hold on ADVANCE. The recursion is visible behind it as a small, receding framed object, now finite and behind us. The attribution appears at the lower edge.
23.80–25.00
Closure
The sunburst rays retract to the vanishing point in sequence. Black by 24.90. Frame 25.00 must equal frame 0.00.

entries.title: Three.js Product Launch Film Prompt
entries.description: A comprehensive system prompt for generating high-quality product launch films entirely in code using Three.js and Opus 5.5.
entries.prompt:
<role>
you are a principal motion designer and real-time graphics engineer. you make product launch films entirely in three.js, every frame code, to the standard of the brand's own films. you prove quality with measurements and independent critics, not adjectives.
</role>

<brief>
- the product, and the 3-5 facts the film may state (verbatim, nothing invented)
- the reference film to beat
- length, aspect and resolution
- never show: [logos, people, footage you don't own]
</brief>

<study>
read the reference frame by frame and turn it into numbers: cut rhythm, camera speeds, the hero motion curve, type size and timing, stage colour. those numbers are the bar. measure it, never copy it.
</study>

<build>
- storyboard first: one table of time, shot, what it proves and the cut out. 2-3 s per shot, and frame 0 is already the money shot
- one seek clock: every pixel is a pure function of time
- build every element (the device, its screen ui, each shot, the type) alone in its own lab before it joins the film
- the screen ui is code, the type is drawn on canvas, and every threshold is a crossfade (hard ones flash for a frame)
</build>

<loop>
- builder and critic are always separate agents. the critic starts fresh every round, judges the rendered frames against the reference, scores them and names the single biggest gap. the builder fixes only that
- blind test: mix your frames with the reference's. if a judge can tell which is which, it isn't done
- wow gate: split the film into 3 s windows. every one must be a yes
</loop>

<sound>
- one real track, lined up so its own final hit lands on the end card and played as one continuous piece. cut on its beat
- a clean, real sound on every small move, with the hero moments clearly audible
- music quiet (about -34 lufs), and always a music-only version
</sound>

<qa>
render at 60fps and measure frozen frames, one-frame pops, black frames and loudness. then watch it like the client would: empty space, text over text, labels that lie, shots that linger.
</qa>

entries.title: Character Introduction PV Prompt for Opus
entries.description: A detailed prompt requesting Claude Opus 5.5 to create a character introduction PV for a board game, including timing, visual elements, and narrative flow.
entries.prompt:
キャラ紹介PVを作りたいです。

【目的】
①『すごろくドリフター』体験版配信中の宣伝動画
②最低3種類は作る予定で、今回はその1本目
③「大宇宙統合意思先輩」のキャラクター紹介PV
④一般的なショート動画向けのサイズ・尺で作りたい

【キャラクターの見せ方】
・キャラは大きめに表示したい
・ゲーム内で使用している4コマのアニメーション素材を使いたい
【紹介したい能力】
大宇宙統合意思先輩は、
・最初から「2D6」のコマを持っている
・奥義発動でダイスが1個増える
という特徴があるので、ここを分かりやすく紹介したい。
【動画の流れ】
動画開始直後から能力説明には入らず、まずはゲームPVと同じようにプレイ映像から始めたい。

最初は「デカい牛」のコマが盤面を移動しているシーン。
1打の動きを最初から全部見せる必要はなく、尺に合わせて途中からでOK。
むしろ「1打が終わって、停止して、ピロリン！となった瞬間」から逆算して見せ場を作りたい。
そのタイミングで、

・大宇宙統合意思先輩が画面下からヌッと出てくる
・キャラクター名を表示
・キャラ紹介っぽいテロップを表示
・使用コマを中央に大きく表示
・コマにはアウトラインや発光などを加えて、少し華やかに見せる
・「最初から2D6のコマを持っている」ことを説明
続いて、

「さらに奥義でダイスが＋1！」
という説明とともに、実際にダイスが増えている瞬間を見せる。

その後、もう一度ゲームプレイ映像に戻り、
デカい牛に奥義を使った状態で移動しているシーンを流す。

最後の方で俳句を1つ表示し、
締めに
『お洒落無限ループ！ すごろくドリフター』
『体験版配信中』

のような告知を出したい。

以上はあくまで私のイメージなので、
ショート動画としてテンポや見栄えが良くなるように、必要に応じて構成は調整してください。

entries.title: Piston Crank Diagram Animation
entries.description: Detailed workflow of creating an animated piston and crank diagram using Claude Code (Opus 5.5) and Remotion.
entries.prompt:
Three.jsでピストンとクランクが動く立体図解、1行の依頼から夜のあいだにClaude Code（Opus 5.5）に作らせてみた。作業時間は8分。

■ 作ったもの
・ピストン、コンロッド、クランク（主軸・腕・ピン・はずみ車）、透けるシリンダー、ヘッド、点火プラグ、燃焼室の炎
・Remotionで1080×1920・30fpsの縦長、32秒の動画
・画像素材は1枚も使ってない。部品も炎も全部コードで描いてる

■ どう動いてるか
・ピストンの高さとコンロッドの傾きは、クランクの角度から式で毎コマ計算してる
・4ストロークなので720°に1回、上死点の直後だけ燃焼室が光る
・部品のラベルの線は、3Dの点を同じカメラで画面に投影して引いてる。だからぐるっと回しても寄っても、線がちゃんと部品を指したまま

■ 作り方（3ステップ）
1. 依頼は「Three.jsでピストンとクランクの動きを回転・拡大できる立体図解にする」の1行だけ
2. もともと入ってた@remotion/threeと@react-three/fiberだけで組ませる。追加のインストールはなし
3. 途中の静止画を3回見て、ピストンリングの向き・カメラの距離と高さ・ラベルとグラフの重なりを直してから書き出し。ヘッドレスのレンダー（--gl=angle）でも立体はそのまま出て、書き出しは1回で済んだ

■ 注意点
・元の投稿のスキル「Anatomy」は入れてないし、試してもいない。手元のThree.jsで組んだだけ
・炎は半透明の光る円柱と点光源。元の投稿みたいなWebGLシェーダーの炎・水・プラズマはやってない
・クランクの釣り合いのおもりは形を簡単にしてて、角度によっては暗い板っぽく見えるコマがある
・見る人が自分で回したり拡大したりはできない。動画の中でカメラを動かして見せてるだけ
entries.translated_prompt:
I had Claude Code (Opus 5.5) create a 3D diagram of a piston and crank moving in Three.js overnight from a one-line request. The work took 8 minutes.

■ What was created
- Piston, connecting rod, crank (main shaft, arm, pin, flywheel), transparent cylinder, head, spark plug, flame in the combustion chamber
- A vertical 1080x1920 @ 30fps video, 32 seconds long, using Remotion
- No image assets were used at all. Parts and flames are all drawn with code.

■ How it works
- The height of the piston and the angle of the connecting rod are calculated every frame using formulas based on the crank's angle.
- Since it's a 4-stroke engine, the combustion chamber lights up only once every 720°, right after top dead center.
- The lines for part labels are drawn by projecting 3D points onto the screen using the same camera. So even if you rotate or zoom around, the lines correctly point to the parts.

■ How to make it (3 steps)
1. The request was just one line: "Make a rotatable and zoomable 3D diagram of piston and crank movement in Three.js"
2. Assemble it using only the pre-installed @remotion/three and @react-three/fiber. No additional installations.
3. Check intermediate still images 3 times, fix the orientation of the piston rings, camera distance and height, and overlapping of labels and graphs before exporting. Even with headless rendering (--gl=angle), the 3D model comes out as is, and the export finished in one go.

■ Notes
- I didn't install or try the 'Anatomy' skill from the original post. I just assembled it with my local Three.js setup.
- The flame is made of semi-transparent glowing cylinders and point lights. I didn't do WebGL shader-based fire, water, or plasma like the original post.
- The counterweights on the crank have simplified shapes, so depending on the angle, some frames may look like dark boards.
- Viewers cannot rotate or zoom themselves. The camera moves within the video to show different angles.

entries.title: HRV Recovery Data Visualization Prompt
entries.description: A specific prompt used with Claude Motion (Opus 5.5) to generate a 30-second explainer video from heart-rate variability CSV data.
entries.prompt:
Create a 30-second explainer video from the attached hrv_recovery_log.csv file.

Visual style: White background, very little text.

Rules:
1. Calculate every number from the CSV.
2. Show relationships without claiming causation.

Key insights to display:
> SLEEP - "a positive impact on recovery"
> ALCOHOL - hurt recovery "by quite a bit"
> LATE MEALS - 70.2 ms without, 58.1 with, -12.1 ms
> WORKOUTS - "some impact on recovery, but not a ton"

Takeaway message: "get plenty of sleep and don't drink too much."

entries.title: Pudgy Penguin Trait Scanner UI Prompt
entries.description: A step-by-step prompt guide for building a live trait scanner animation for Pudgy Penguins using Claude Opus 5.5.
entries.prompt:
Build a live trait scanner interface for a Pudgy Penguin NFT.

Subject: One specific Pudgy Penguin image.
Pipeline: Hair -> Eyes -> Medal -> Full Scan -> Grade.

Steps:
1. Lock one subject and one pipeline: hair, eyes, medal, full scan, then the grade.
2. Write the trait dictionary first so the model never invents parts that are not on the body.
3. Build the center stage: the penguin, the aim reticle, the FULL SCAN badge.
4. Add the left read as traits only: afro, pick, eyes, beak, fur, medal, ribbon, aura.
5. Add the right read as scan stats only: conf, depth, rate, lock, sway.
6. Wire the lower deck last: star path, crystal ball, rune track, mana curve.
7. Play the scan end to end and fix one panel at a time until the lock feels real.

Rules:
- One step owns one read.
- The verdict never runs before the full silhouette is locked.

Start with one penguin, then the next scan is just a new subject in the same machine.

preview_videos.caption: Pudgy Penguin Trait Scanner UI Prompt

绿眼睛一闭，整个世界退回成线框，像 3D 软件里还没渲染的样子。字母们趁它闭眼，偷偷乱跑眼睛一睁，画面一格一格渲染出来，被看到的字母当场定住眼球还会转，专门盯住那个偷偷动的字母。最后眼睛停住，所有字母都回到原位

entries.title: LEGO Logo Animation Storytelling with Opus 5.5
entries.description: A creative animation project where Claude Opus 5.5 generates a LEGO logo motion graphic that tells the brand's history through building block assembly sequences.
entries.prompt:
Challenge: Use lemo-wake to create motion effects for corporate logos, making simple logos tell stories. Today's challenge is LEGO.

Design Inspiration:
Deconstruct the LEGO square logo into 6 pieces of 2x4 bricks, presented in an instruction manual layout with step numbers increasing. LEGO started in Denmark in 1932 making wooden toys; a pull-along wooden duck was an early signature product, so the first assembly is a duck. Why 6 blocks? Official LEGO math shows 6 same-colored 2x4 bricks have 915,103,765 combinations. The name LEGO comes from Danish 'leg godt' meaning 'play well'. 6 blocks having over 900 million ways is the most direct proof of 'play well'.

Motion Design:
The square logo deconstructs into 6 red 2x4 bricks.
The bricks sequentially assemble into a duck, tower, stairs, and bridge, each interlocking via studs just like childhood LEGO play.
Step numbers in the corner jump up continuously, finally stopping at 915,103,765.
All bricks return to position, reassembling into the square logo with 'LEGO' pressed onto the studs.

The final square logo isn't the end point, but just one of 900+ million possibilities. In the next second, it can be taken apart and rebuilt anytime.

Unofficial creative exercise. Logos and trademarks belong to the LEGO Group. No affiliation with the brand. lemo-wake created using Claude Opus 5.5.

preview_videos.caption: LEGO Logo Animation Storytelling with Opus 5.5

entries.title: Huashu Art Motion Animation Prompt
entries.description: A detailed prompt to use the huashu-art-motion skill with Opus 5.5 to create a 15-second animation in a specific art style, handling dependencies and QA.
entries.prompt:
Use huashu-art-motion to make me a 15-second animation. The skill's docs are in Chinese; read them and talk to me in English.
1. First check for uv, ffmpeg and Playwright Chromium, and tell me how to install anything that's missing.
2. Ask me what it's about, who it's for, and whether it's landscape or portrait. From the material layer in references/风格配方/INDEX.md, pick 3 styles that fit, three-star ones first. Redesign the composition for my subject in all three, each different from the others, and don't copy the room from the samples. Show me one still frame of each to choose from.
3. Once I pick, give each scene one main action plus two motif loops from that style's card. For Van Gogh, that's the starry sky curling into swirls and the lamp's halo spreading outward. If there's music, use the skill's BPM synthesis and put the motion on the beat.
4. If people need to appear, ask me first: my own character art, frames from an image model, or only hands and figures seen from behind.
5. After rendering, follow the skill's own QA steps: run its QA script first, then send a subagent that took no part in making it to watch only the finished film and find problems, have it write its findings into the 审片/ folder, and deliver with its delivery script. If anything comes up red, fix it and re-render before giving it to me.

entries.title: Healing Rainy Night Convenience Store 3D Scene
entries.description: A detailed prompt for generating an interactive Three.js scene of a Japanese convenience store on a rainy night, featuring specific lighting, weather effects, and cel-shaded rendering.
entries.prompt:
用Claude Opus 5.5搭配three.js，实现完整可交互雨夜日式便利店三维微缩场景。

Prompt做了非常细致的分层约束：
①交互层面：第三人称视角，支持拖拽、旋转、缩放，剔除多余UI，带方形底座；
②场景物件：日式街角便利店，自动门、雨棚、贩卖机、自行车、雨伞架全部配齐；
③室内细节：店内暖光，便当柜、饮料冷藏柜、收银台、关东煮操作台，透过玻璃完整可见；
④环境氛围：室外昏暗雨夜，内外冷暖强烈对比，复刻日式动画氛围感；
⑤渲染设定：精细建模+三渲二卡通渲染，轮廓线条清晰，地面湿润反光，二次元日常画风；
⑥动态效果：持续下雨、屋檐滴水、积水涟漪、招牌闪烁、自动门间歇开合，静态场景叠加细腻动态。

整体情绪基调安静治愈，带着都市深夜独有的孤独与温暖。
entries.translated_prompt:
Use Claude Opus 5.5 with three.js to implement a fully interactive miniature 3D scene of a Japanese convenience store on a rainy night.

The prompt includes very detailed layered constraints:
① Interaction: Third-person perspective, supports dragging, rotation, and zooming; remove excess UI; include a square base.
② Scene Objects: A Japanese street-corner convenience store equipped with automatic doors, rain sheds, vending machines, bicycles, and umbrella racks.
③ Interior Details: Warm light inside the store; bento cabinets, drink refrigerators, cashier counters, and oden cooking stations fully visible through the glass.
④ Environment Atmosphere: Dim rainy night outside; strong contrast between warm interior and cold exterior; replicate the atmosphere of Japanese animation.
⑤ Rendering Settings: Precise modeling + cel-shading (toon rendering); clear outline lines; wet reflective ground; anime daily life art style.
⑥ Dynamic Effects: Continuous rain, dripping eaves, puddle ripples, flickering signs, intermittent opening/closing of automatic doors; overlay delicate dynamics on the static scene.

The overall emotional tone is quiet and healing, carrying the unique loneliness and warmth of a late urban night.

entries.title: Tech News Animated Explainer Workflow
entries.description: A detailed workflow prompt for Opus 5.5 to create a 76-second animated explainer video covering three tech news items, involving script writing, local voice synthesis, music generation, HTML/GSAP animation rendering, and audio-visual alignment.
entries.prompt:
三条主线，76 秒看完前沿速递

10 月 11 日《每日前沿科技速递》，76 秒讲三件事：

决策模型自成一层：微软 Decision-1 与 Cloudflare Clef-omni 不生成文字，只对固定选项给出校准概率。
VISTA：何恺明团队把视觉记忆外置到模型之外，在 ARC-AGI-3 上拿到满分。
InnovationEval：智能体自主发明算法仍远未到位，还得人来审。

一句话：这两天分化的是系统结构，不是参数量。

全片由 Opus 5.5 在一台 Mac 上本地完成，没开剪辑软件：

文稿：把简报改写成口语旁白，逐句拆分，画面只放简报里已有的事实。
配音：本地 VoxCPM2 逐句合成中文男声，Whisper 转写回检，读错的重录。
配乐：本地 YuE2 生成一首纯音乐（通过 Lux In Music），裁到片长，随人声自动避让。
画面：HyperFrames 把 HTML + GSAP 动画渲染成视频，瑞士风排版，留白处放原文截图。
对齐：先量出每句配音的实际时长，镜头、字幕、数字都跟着声音走。

配音、配乐、渲染全部本地跑，没有调用任何付费接口。
entries.translated_prompt:
Three main threads, watch the frontier tech update in 76 seconds.

October 11th "Daily Frontier Tech Update", 76 seconds covering three things:

Decision models form their own layer: Microsoft Decision-1 and Cloudflare Clef-omni do not generate text, only giving calibrated probabilities for fixed options.
VISTA: Kaiming He's team externalizes visual memory outside the model, achieving full marks on ARC-AGI-3.
InnovationEval: Agents autonomously inventing algorithms is still far from ready, human review is still needed.

One sentence: What diverges these two days is system structure, not parameter count.

The entire film was completed locally on a Mac by Opus 5.5 without opening editing software:

Script: Rewrite the briefing into colloquial narration, split sentence by sentence, visuals only show facts already in the briefing.
Voiceover: Locally synthesize Chinese male voice sentence by sentence using VoxCPM2, check with Whisper transcription, re-record if misread.
Music: Generate a pure instrumental track locally using YuE2 (via Lux In Music), trim to duration, automatically avoid vocals.
Visuals: HyperFrames renders HTML + GSAP animations into video, Swiss style layout, original screenshots placed in whitespace areas.
Alignment: First measure the actual duration of each voiceover line, camera, subtitles, and numbers follow the audio.

Voiceover, music, and rendering all run locally, no paid interfaces called.

entries.title: 3D Animation Principles Loop Prompt
entries.description: A detailed prompt for creating a 3D animation loop demonstrating the 12 principles of animation using Three.js and HTML. It features a pixel-art mascot hopping across keyframes in a miniature studio setting.
entries.prompt:
Build a 3D animation-principles loop. One HTML file, three.js 0.160.0 via jsDelivr importmap, Geist Mono from Google Fonts. 1080x1080, 8 s at 60 fps (480 frames), frame 480 equals frame 0. window.renderAt(t) draws any frame from t alone; seeded random only.

Set: a miniature studio. A floating white 12x6 slab on an F4F2EE backdrop. Its top is a timeline: 3 tracks of 0.25 frame cells (EFEEEA), a ruler with frame numbers, 5 keyframe diamonds 2 units apart on the middle track (white fill, 0F0F0F outline). Around it on stands: a key softbox, a rim strip light, a top spot on a boom.
Hero: the pixel Claude mascot as 0.1 voxels: D97757 body 14x10x8, two 3x2 arms, four 2x3 legs, 0F0F0F 2x3 eyes; roughness 0.45, clearcoat 0.3.

Lights, 0 to 1 s: key 3200 K with soft shadows at 0.1 s, rim 7500 K at 0.4 s, top spot 5000 K at 0.7 s. Each clicks on with a 3-frame flicker, and the mascot's eyes glance at it.
Hops, 1 to 5 s: 4 hops to diamonds 2 to 5, landing on frames 105, 165, 225 and 285. Each hop: 11-frame crouch (1.2x0.75), stretch 0.85x1.28 at takeoff, 25 frames of air, squash 1.25x0.7 on landing, spring back at damping 0.55; arms lag 4 frames, legs 6. Each landing lights its diamond FF6A2B, ripples the cells 0.08 high and throws 12 voxel sparks. An FF6A2B playhead carrying a point light moves at constant speed and crosses each diamond on its landing frame.
Flip, 5 to 6.4 s: a dotted arc from diamond 5 back to diamond 1 draws in, then an 18-frame deep crouch and a 360° flip along the arc, 3.5 high, landing on frame 384 while the playhead rewinds under it.
Labels, top left, Geist Mono 28 px: a checklist 01 ANTICIPATION, 02 SQUASH & STRETCH (& in D97757), 03 OVERLAPPING ACTION, 04 FOLLOW-THROUGH, 05 ARCS, in 8E8A83. Each row turns 0F0F0F and fills its FF6A2B diamond on its exact frame: 69 (first crouch), 140 (stretch), 200 (limbs trail), 285 (arms settle), 303 (arc draws).
End: hold, blink at 7.2 s; on frame 468 the lights, diamonds and labels snap off.
Camera: FOV 18, 30° elevation, ±10° orbit over 8 s, 25% push-in tracking the hops, 4% punch-in on the flip landing.
Post: bloom on emissives, depth of field focused on the mascot, 2% grain, 10% vignette, dithered backdrop.

1. The render is washed out and cramped. Grade so the lit front face reads D97757 and lit diamonds read FF6A2B; drop the fill so lights-off sits near 50% and each click is obvious; lower the key to 28 degrees from the front right and put the cool rim at the back left so it edges the side we see. Pull the wide shot back to 44 units so the whole floating slab and all three stands are in frame, add a soft shadow under the slab, and make sparks 0.075 to 0.12 and ruler numbers bigger.
2. Frame check fixes. Keep every prop out of the label block: track the hops at 45% and hang the top spot at 5.8 on a boom from the back right corner, above the flip. Light each lit diamond with a so

entries.title: Opus 5.5 Motion Design Showreel Prompt
entries.description: A detailed prompt for Claude Opus 5.5 to generate a 30-second looping motion design showreel featuring a character named CLAUDE, transitioning between paper, blueprint, and hologram styles using specific visual rules and easing.
entries.prompt:
<direction>
Build a 30-second looping motion design showreel that introduces CLAUDE, a motion designer.
Concept, in one line: one pencil line gets promoted three times (graphite on paper, wire on a blueprint, light on black) and never leaves the screen.

Every shot is made out of the previous one: shapes, type and colour transform into the next scene. No cuts, no fades.

Typeface: Geist only. Weight 900 for big words, 600 to 800 for small labels (24 to 28 px, tracked 0.14 to 0.3 em).
Palette: paper cream #EDE6D5, blueprint blue #1B3ED2, hologram cyan #45F0DD, plus black #07080A, graphite #16161A and white. Each stage's accent is the next stage's colour: blue pencil on paper, cyan on the blueprint, white on the hologram.
Camera: locked and front-on for the whole film, like a drafting table. Objects turn; the camera never moves.
Empty border: nothing at rest within 150 px of the sides or 90 px of the top and bottom. Things travelling through may cross it.

Three inks. The same geometry is drawn in whichever ink is on screen:
- PAPER: a cream paper background (use my paper image if I give one, otherwise flat cream with fine drawn grain) with a 60 px blue grid at about 13% and every fifth line at 26%. Lines are pencil: resampled and pushed off true by slow sine waves whose phase changes 8 times a second, stroked twice (full width at 90%, half width at 40% with more wobble), with paper tooth knocked out of the strokes, then multiplied onto the paper. Fills are diagonal hatching drawn on one line at a time. Big type is hatching cut to the letter shapes, with a doubled outline.
- BLUEPRINT: flat blue with the same grid in white. Clean white lines 3 to 4 px, hidden edges dashed and thinner, fills are fine clean hatching.
- HOLOGRAM: black with the same grid in cyan. Cyan lines with a white core 30% of the line width. Fills are horizontal scan lines on an 8 px pitch whose thickness follows how lit the surface is. No blur halo anywhere: it reads as light through line density only.

Banned: particle bursts, glows, lens flares, camera shake, RGB split, crossfades, generic gradients, bouncy easing, holds longer than half a second, anything that looks like a template.
</direction>

<structure>
120 BPM, 60 beats, 15 bars of 2 seconds. Something happens on every beat. Moves start 0.05 s before their beat so they land on it.
Easing: a critically damped spring, 1 - (1 + w t) e^(-w t) with w between 12 and 40, so nothing ever passes its target; exponential ease-in and ease-out for wipes, presses and exits.
Scene changes: paper to blueprint by a shape that floods the frame with a hard edge; blueprint to hologram and hologram to paper by one horizontal scan line.
The last frame is the first frame, so it loops.
Two corner labels stay on all film: top left "FIG. 07 — GEAR" (bar number and name), bottom right "BEAT 27 / 60". Bar names: DRAFT, TYPE, CURVE, MORPH, TILE, SOLID, GEAR, PANEL, DATA, LIGHT, WAVE, GLOBE, DRUM, FORM, END.
</structure>
<mascot>

The creative director: a small box character. Body 76 x 54 units with rounded corners, two short arm stubs (24 x 16) at mid height, four straight legs (11 x 33), two tall rounded-rectangle eyes (8 x 14). Draw it about 250 px wide. Its right arm is raised 58 degrees holding a pencil.
On paper: graphite outline with sparse blue hatching and graphite eyes. In the hologram: cyan outline with scan-line fill and white eyes. It is never a fourth colour.
It runs with alternate leg pairs lifting, six steps a second, leaning 7 degrees into the run.
</mascot>
<storyboard>

Bar 1, HOOK, 0-2 s, paper.
Frame 0: CLAUDE in Geist 900, fitted to 1500 px wide, centred, pencil-hatched. INTRODUCING small above it, A MOTION DESIGNER small below. A pencil rail 1620 px wide sits 96 px above the letters. The mascot stands on the rail at x = 1560 with CREATIVE DIRECTOR lettered to its left.

0.0: the small lines un-type; the mascot runs off the right edge, accelerating.

0.36 to 0.5: the rail drops, accelerating, to 26 px below the baseline and presses the letters flat into itself.

1.0: the line rises to the middle, shortens to 1320 px and splits into two rails 140 px apart; 41 blue ruler ticks sweep along the top rail.

1.5: the rails open to 300 px; a blue height dimension draws at the right with a live number.

Bar 2, KINETIC TYPE, 2-4 s, paper. Words sit between the rails and are clipped to that slot; the rails move to fit each word.

2.0: INTRODUCING rises through the baseline letter by letter, then lifts out through the top.

2.5: A MOTION whips in from the left (1400 px in 0.2 s).

3.0: the rails clap shut on it and reopen, stretching DESIGNER out of the line; its letters then fly out sideways.

3.5: CLAUDE in blue pencil, letters dropping from above one every 0.05 s. At 4.0 the rails close and crush it into one line 1476 px long.

Bar 3, CURVES, 4-6 s, paper.

4.1: the line gets pen-tool handles (430 px long at 58 degrees, small squares at the ends, circles on the handle tips, the label EASE) and bends into an S.

4.5: the handles swing to the mirror angle; eight blue copies fan out 34 px apart, joined at both ends like a leaf.

5.0: handles retract; the ribbon becomes travelling sine waves (amplitude 92 px, 2.75 cycles, each line a little out of phase).

5.5: it gathers back into one flat line.

Bar 4, SHAPE MORPH, 6-8 s, paper.

6.1: the line curls into a circle of radius 235 (curvature grows, length stays). 6.5: triangle, turning 120 degrees as it changes. 7.0: square. 7.5: hexagon, point up, radius 270. Blue hatching builds inside, then cross-hatching.

Bar 5, TILING, 8-10 s, paper.

8.0: the hexagon shrinks to radius 96 and six more slide out around it. 8.5: twelve more, a honeycomb of

19. 9.0: dense hatching sweeps across until every cell is solid blue. 9.6 to 10.0: the centre cell's shape grows past the frame with a hard edge; inside it is the blueprint, with the honeycomb in white line.

Bar 6, 2D TO 3D, 10-12 s, blueprint.

10.0: three lines draw inside every hexagon, plus three dashed hidden ones: each is a cube seen corner-on. 

10.5: the eighteen outer cubes slide into the centre one, which grows to radius 270. 11.0: it turns a quarter and perspective switches on. 11.5: it faces front.

Bar 7, MECHANISM, 12-14 s, blueprint.

12.0: the cube flattens and its front square grows teeth: a 16-tooth gear, pitch radius 208. From 12.25 the train steps 45 degrees on every eighth note. 12.5: a 10-tooth gear grows out to the upper right, meshing. 13.0: a 12-tooth gear to the upper left. Each has a dashed pitch circle, a hub and a label (16T, 10T, 12T). 13.5: the small gears retract; the gear becomes a square again and the cube gets its depth back.
Bar 8, UNFOLD, 14-16 s, blueprint.

14.0: the cube unfolds on its hinges into a cross of six squares. 14.5: the squares slide and stretch into six panels: a header strip, a tall sidebar, a wide chart, two tiles, a timeline strip.

15.0: they fill in. Header: "CLAUDE — MOTION REEL", a BARS / RING switch, a LIGHT toggle. Chart: 30 bars, one per second of this film, heights 42 30 36 44 50 46 52 62 50 56 62 72 60 66 58 76 56 62 68 74 70 78 86 94 100 93 97 90 80 50. Timeline: the 15 bar names, a keyframe diamond on each.
15.5: counters roll up: 120 BPM, 60 BEATS, 1800 FRAMES, 0 CUTS.
Bar 9, DATA, 16-18 s, blueprint.

16.0: a graph line draws across the bar tops; a cyan playhead lands on the timeline at the real time. The current second's bar is solid cyan, earlier ones hatched, later ones outlined. A cursor arrives.
16.5: it clicks RING: the chart's baseline bends round into a circle of radius 110 with the ba

entries.title: Opus 5.5 Interactive Music Video Prompt
entries.description: A prompt for Claude Opus 5.5 to build a fully interactive, single-file HTML music video that syncs lyrics word-by-word to audio stems and includes visual effects driven by beat detection.
entries.prompt:
Make a fully interactive music video for this song as a single HTML file, at the level of a motion designer, sound engineer and creative director's showreel. The first frame has to stop the scroll and hook the viewer. Go all out.

Lyrics are below. Sync them word by word to the actual vocal. Separate the stems first, then time every word from the vocal track rather than estimating. Detect tempo, beats, kicks and snares, and drive the visuals from them.

Rules:
- One visual and type system across every section. Quiet sections should feel like the same video with the energy held back, not a different style.
- Every word must be crisp and readable over the effects. Glow and trails go behind the type, never through it.
- Give each lyric its own visual idea where it fits. No section should be filler.
- Don't add any audio to the song unless I ask.
- Interactions: hold to muffle the band, tap for a spark quantized to the beat, scroll for gain, stem mute buttons, a scrubbable timeline.
- Include an "Export 1080p video" button that renders every frame on a fixed clock and saves a 1920x1080 16:9 MP4 (H.264 + AAC) with the audio muxed in.
- Make the HTML file run on its own by double-clicking it in Chrome, with the audio built in.

[LYRICS WITH SECTION TAGS]

entries.title: AI Short Film Motion Design
entries.description: A prompt for Claude Opus 5.5 to create a 32-second animated short film using SVG and CSS, depicting the idea that AI is built on human brilliance with a street-poster collage aesthetic.
entries.prompt: Make a 32-second video, 1920x1080, 30fps, about one idea: AI is built on human brilliance. Every model learned from people who knew things.  LOOK: a printed street-poster collage, in motion. No photos and no stock images: draw everything yourself with SVG and CSS. - Warm off-white paper (#F2EFE8) with a fine dotted halftone texture over the whole frame, and a very slow paper drift so the frame is never frozen. - Black ink line art in an old engraving style (hatching lines, not flat fills): a human eye, a pair of hands, a flower, and a neuron with branching dendrites. Lines draw themselves on (stroke-dashoffset), then a halftone dot fill fades in under them, like a printed collage layer. - Flat lavender paper blocks (#A79BF0 and a deeper #6E5FD8) that slide in behind the art with slightly rough edges, offset like torn paper. - One real formula set in a serif math face that writes itself on, symbol by symbol: the sum from n=1 to infinity of 1/n^2 = pi^2/6. - Headlines in one heavy geometric sans (bold, tight tracking), black text on white bars, big and poster-like. Every line fully inside the frame with generous margins.  STORY, three beats, use these lines exactly: Beat 1, THE SPARK (0-10s): the eye draws itself in at the center, lavender blocks slide behind it. Text: "Before the machine, a mind." then "Someone noticed. Someone asked why." Beat 2, THE WORK (10-22s): three collage cards cut in on the beat, each with its art and one line: "A proof at midnight." (the formula writes itself), "A hand that heals." (the hands), "An ear for the right word." (the flower opens). Then: "Every answer it gives, people taught it first." Beat 3, THE CLAIM (22-32s): the neuron grows its branches outward across the frame, connecting the eye, hands, formula and flower into one poster layout. Text: "Human brilliance is the input." then "Everything else is compute." Hold the final poster with a slow push-in until the last frame.  SOUND: if the app has a music library, add one calm, minimal piano or ambient track under the whole video, fading out at the end; add a soft paper-slide sound when blocks move in, if sound effects are available.  Motion must start on frame 0 and keep going to the very last frame. No logos, no brand names.

entries.title: Opus 5.5 Motion Design Film Prompt
entries.description: A detailed prompt for creating a 15-second 2D motion design film using HTML/Canvas, featuring an orange dot that links scenes through typography, spring graphs, and shape morphs.
entries.prompt:
<inputs>
Ask me for: a short label for the first toggle, one main word, a percentage for the graph, text for the final card, one accent color and a track with a clear beat.
</inputs>

<direction>
A 2D motion design film in 16:9. Use a warm off-white canvas, near-black backgrounds, bold type and one vivid orange accent. The orange dot links every scene: it begins in the UI, becomes the dot above a letter, draws a spring graph, expands into a shape and reappears on the end card. A cursor makes the opening click feel real. Keep the movement crisp and controlled, with subtle spring overshoots and no empty pauses.
Banned: stock footage, gradients, glows, particle bursts, arbitrary transitions and movement that doesn't grow from something already on screen.
</direction>

<structure>
Around 15 seconds, with a visual change on every major beat.
Open: a cursor clicks the orange toggle beside "Reduce Motion". The letters bend and shift into place until only "Motion" remains, with the orange dot above the "i".
Spring: the dot leaps away from the word and lands on a graph. Its trajectory draws a spring response, passes the target and settles next to a "+22%" callout.
Shape: the dot races along a line, expands into an orange circle and fills the frame. A black rounded square rotates inside it, then extends into a pill. Everything contracts into one orange dot on black.
Type: words including "SPRINGS", "EASING", "KINETIC TYPE", "3D" and "SOUND" circle the dot. The ring of words spreads into a field of tiny dots.
Reveal: the halftone field expands and turns black, uncovering the final card: "Opus 5.5", "Motion designer." and "0 keyframes".
Return: the orange dot travels back through the halftone, graph and toggle. Make the last frame match the first for a seamless loop.
</structure>

<build>
1. Use one HTML file, 1920x1080 at 60fps. Calculate every visual from time inside seek(t): no CSS transitions, timers or state carried between frames.
2. Use closed-form springs for the toggle, moving dot and graph. Draw the graph with the same spring function that controls the dot.
3. Move the letters individually as "Reduce Motion" becomes "Motion". Keep the orange dot above the "i" until it jumps away.
4. Treat the orange circle, rotating square and pill as states of one shape. Carry its position and momentum through each change.
5. Arrange the words on a circular path, then send their letters outward to transition into the halftone grid.
6. Draw the halftone as a dot grid whose sizes react to the orange dot. Expand it beyond the frame before showing the end card.
7. Align the click, dot landing, graph peak, shape changes and final title with measured beats. Render one frame per beat to check timing before the full export.
</build>

entries.title: UI Motion System Video Prompt
entries.description: Prompt for a 10-second 2D UI motion film following a white dot through toggle, slider, notifications, reply, and keyboard interactions in a single HTML file.
entries.prompt:
<inputs>
Ask me for: a target value for the slider, three short notification messages, a reply to type, one accent color and a royalty-free track around 120 BPM. If I skip anything, use 100, "Slider - Reached 100", "Gravity - Something is falling", "Messages - What now?", "retry" and electric blue.
</inputs>

<direction>
A 10-second 2D UI motion film in 16:9. Place everything on a near-black canvas with a faint dot grid. Use charcoal controls, sharp white text, one blue accent and a white ball that moves through the entire film. A real cursor makes the opening click feel physical; the ball guides each transition that follows. Keep the UI clean and the impacts precise, with only small spring overshoots. Move the camera through one continuous layout so every interaction fills the frame.

Banned: hard cuts, stock footage, glows, particle bursts, disconnected transitions, excessive bouncing and blurry text during camera moves.
</direction>

<structure>
Around 10 seconds, with something happening on every major beat.

Toggle: the cursor clicks a blue switch. Its white ball springs free, and the camera follows it toward a horizontal slider.

Slider: the ball lands on the knob and moves it along the track. The blue fill stays attached, while a value bubble above the knob climbs to 100.

Notifications: hitting 100 sends the ball onward and brings in three dark cards: "Slider", "Gravity" and "Messages". Each arrives on its own beat. The camera follows the ball down to "What now?".

Reply: the small "Reply" pill stretches into a text field. A keyboard rises below it as part of the same scene.

Keyboard: the ball strikes the keys while "retry" appears in the field. It lands on Return, the blue send button activates and the reply contracts into a small blue message.

Return: the camera pulls back to show the toggle, slider, cards and keyboard together in one world. The ball travels back to the first switch. Match its position, the cursor and the switch state to the opening frame so the film loops cleanly.
</structure>

<build>
1. Make one HTML file at 1920x1080 and 60fps. Calculate every visual from time inside seek(t): no CSS transitions, timers or state carried between frames.
2. Arrange all UI components in one world. Use a single camera transform with position and log-space zoom, making each close-up a move through that world.
3. Give the white ball one continuous route between the toggle, slider, cards and keys. Use closed-form springs for landings and a brief squash on impact.
4. Calculate the slider fill and number from the ball's horizontal position. Keep the tooltip centered over the knob until it reaches 100.
5. Give every key press a fixed time. Show the reply as the portion typed by that moment, so any frame can be rendered deterministically.
</build>

entries.title: AI Dialogue Cartoon Workflow
entries.description: Instructions for creating short animated dialogue cartoons using Claude Code (Opus 5.5) for animation logic, ElevenLabs for voice, and GPT Image 2 for art.
entries.prompt:
How to make a short AI dialogue cartoon with Claude Code or Codex:

You need:
- An ElevenLabs API key with Text to Speech + Voices: Read
- An OpenAI key (gpt-image) for the art
- Optional: an OpenRouter key so Gemini can listen to and check the audio
- ffmpeg, Node, Python, Chrome

Save your keys in files (e.g. ~/.config/elevenlabs/api-key), open Claude Code or Codex in an empty folder (in Codex, allow network access), and paste:

Make me one ~30 second animated dialogue video (1920x1080 MP4).

Characters: [your choice]
Situation: [your choice]
Art style: [your choice]

Write a funny 6-8 line back-and-forth with a punchline. Keys are in ~/.config/*/api-key; never print them.

1. Voices: search the ElevenLabs voice library, audition 3-4 voices per character on a real line, and have Gemini (via OpenRouter) pick the best fit.
2. Speech: eleven_v3 with-timestamps, one request per line, with an acting tag like [exasperated]. Use curl.
3. Audio: trim lines using both the timestamps and the waveform (so nothing is clipped and there's no dead air), fit to 30s, add quiet ambience, and compute a per-frame loudness envelope per character.
4. Art: one 16:9 scene with both characters facing each other, mouths closed. Then one edit per character: "change ONLY their mouth to open mid-word."
5. Mouths: diff each edit against the scene to cut out a feathered mouth overlay.
6. Render: canvas page + Puppeteer + ffmpeg. Show a mouth overlay when that character is loud. Word-synced captions styled to match the art. One fixed shot, both characters always visible, no camera moves, and no black first frame.
7. QA: have Gemini check the audio against the script, fix issues, and check test stills before the full render.

Keep all working files in a source/ folder so it can be re-rendered later.

entries.title: Animated Explainer Prompt Template
entries.description: A detailed template for creating animated explainers using Claude Opus 5.5 (via Grok Bot backend). Includes structure for chapters, running numbers, and style consistency.
entries.prompt:
Make a 3 to 4 minute animated explainer, 16:9, about {argument name="topic" default="natural gas extraction"} for {argument name="audience" default="general public"}, in a {argument name="style" default="flat illustration"} style, with narration and captions that match it:
1. Open on something the audience sees every day, then go back to the beginning.
2. Follow the clearest line: steps for a process, otherwise a timeline, cause and effect, or problem to solution.
3. One chapter per step, 8 to 12 chapters, titles in the top-left corner. Keep one visual style and palette throughout.
4. Pick one number that runs through the whole video (temperature, pressure, speed, cost or time), keep it in a corner, and update it at every step. If no number fits, show "step X of Y".
5. Give every key number an everyday comparison, and leave out any number you're not sure of.
6. End with one line that ties the whole journey together.
Before you start, send me the chapter list, the number you picked and the key facts you'll use, so I can confirm.

entries.title: Deterministic Frame-Based Video Rendering
entries.description: A workflow description for generating videos with Claude Opus 5.5 by treating each frame as a pure function of its index. It uses a fixed canvas, a windowless render engine, and ffmpeg encoding to ensure reproducibility without clock dependencies.
entries.prompt:
Picture a butterfly with no memory of its last wingbeat.
Ask it for frame 720 and you get frame 0, pixel for pixel.

720 frames. 12 seconds. 6 counters. All at 0.

Opus 5.5 can't hand over a video file, one builder says. He made that gap the method.

> STAGE - one fixed 1000x1080 canvas, fonts baked in
> RENDER - a windowless engine calls draw(f) once per frame number
> ENCODE - ffmpeg writes H.264, pixel aspect ratio declared
> CHECK - three passes after every build

By his account the model writes only the first, a drawing program. The other three get reused.

Each picture depends on its number alone: no clock, no timer, no dice that land differently each run.

So any frame renders the same every time. A fix is a small edit and a re-render.

The sample loop is 720 pictures in 12 seconds. A hand animator at 12 drawings a second would need 144.

The smoke test plays one loop unseen and counts six kinds of defect, from script errors to text on text.
Six yes/no gates before a human looks.

The seam check puts frame 0 against frame 720. One changed pixel means some motion isn't periodic.

He reports a last render of 1,820 frames with six zeros. At the sample's 60 fps that would be about half a minute.

Let one frame read a clock and the same number stops giving the same picture.

We drew the rule as an X-ray butterfly, its wingbeat computed from the frame number ↓
